title: Choose this day (Joshua 24:15)
hookLine: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD"

lines: THEN JOSHUA ASKS THEM TO DECIDE.
cards: Joshua's farewell begins with an awkward piece of family history. All the tribes are gathered at Shechem, elders, heads, judges, officers.
And the story he tells starts further back than anyone might expect, before Abraham. Your fathers, he says, Terah, the father of Abraham, lived beyond the River, and served other gods.
The people's history doesn't begin with faith. It begins with a man taken out of one life and led into another. Joshua tells it all, up to this moment.
Then he stops, and asks the whole people to decide.

teach.h: I TOOK, I SENT, I GAVE: ALL OF IT A GIFT.
teach.b: For most of the speech, Joshua speaks in God's voice. I took your father Abraham. I sent Moses and Aaron.
I brought you out. I gave you a land you didn't labor for, cities you didn't build, vineyards and olive groves you didn't plant. Everything they have arrives as a gift.
Then, in his own voice, he urges them to serve the Lord and put away the other gods.
And then, strangely, he hands them the choice anyway: if serving the Lord seems wrong to you, "choose you this day whom ye will serve."
The gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the land you live in now. And he says where he stands: "but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."
The people answer at once: far be it from us to forsake the Lord. Then Joshua pushes back. You can't serve the Lord, he says; he is a holy God.
Some readers hear a test: a choice made too quickly is easy to drop, so he makes them choose again, slowly. They do: no, they say, we will serve the Lord.

teach.h: AS FOR ME AND MY HOUSE.
teach.b: Then you are witnesses against yourselves, he tells them, and they reply in one breath: we are witnesses.
Joshua writes the words in a book, and sets up a great stone under the oak at Shechem, saying the stone has heard everything. Soon after, Joshua dies, and the book draws to a close.
The choice isn't made once, for all time, by a leader. Each generation stands at its own Shechem.

how: Jews read Joshua 24, the covenant at Shechem and the death of Joshua, as the close of the book of Joshua; the chapter's retelling of history, starting with Terah, is studied alongside other passages where the people's story is told aloud.

practice: Your house might be a family, a roommate, a partner, or just you and a kettle.
Let one small question come up that keeps getting put off, when you eat together, how you speak when you're tired, what happens on the day of rest, and choose one thing.
Say it inside, in Joshua's shape, and finish the sentence: as for me and my house, we will.

wordCard.voice: Shechem. Where Joshua gave his last words: here are the options, here is where I stand, now you decide, and decide again. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the stone has heard everything. A choice can have a date and a place. See you tomorrow.
